eras.label: Mapped village · auto T1 with mapped pit rims
eras.summary: Matmata el Qadima, a Berber village of pit dwellings: each house is a courtyard dug into the ground, with rooms cut into the courtyard walls. 26 courtyard pits are mapped in OpenStreetMap as rim outlines (natural=cliff with building=yes) and are drawn as holes in the ground.
eras.basis: Pit rims, buildings, walls and paths are traced from OpenStreetMap (ODbL); the ground is the Terrarium terrain model (~30 m source resolution). Kalaa Matmata, the ruined hilltop above the village, is a separate row (matmata-kalaa-n11034987883).
eras.conjecture: No pit depth is mapped, so every pit is drawn 7 m deep to a flat floor. Published descriptions give the courtyards as 5-10 m across and no deeper than about 9 m (Fabrizi 2023, MAT-01), or about 9 m across and as deep (BME Habitatio, MAT-02). The rooms, tunnels and stairs inside the pits are not drawn: none are mapped. Walls without a height tag use the programme's schematic 6 m; buildings use 4 m.
